column1: # KeyCode batch: owner <TAB> kind <TAB> old <TAB> descriptor <TAB> semantic name
# Evidence is on the declaration line itself: every constant carries its own libGDX key code and
# its own display label, e.g. a(29,"A"), z(54,"Z"), A(62,"SPACE"), B(21,"LEFT"). 29..54 are the
# libGDX Input.Keys codes for A..Z, so the 26 lowercase constants are KEY_A..KEY_Z and the five
# uppercase ones are SPACE/LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN. Prefixing the letters keeps them distinct from the
# five direction constants, which the batch renames in the same pass.
# Fields and methods are pinned by their bodies:
#   F is the int compared with UserConfig.getActionKey*() -> keyCode
#   G is the string shown in the options list boxes       -> label
#   a() returns F -> getKeyCode   b() returns G -> getLabel
# No reference is name-based: every call site is KeyCode.values()[i], and the config stores the
# int key code, so renaming cannot change saved data. Requires RenameAst to accept
